{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjqe88AAAABZimz6Q", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3INzhDJY8M", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IN", "number": 115, "title": "Add evidence-qualified read-only resident-profile lookup to mail and OLT", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `b75606a0ca47d62d5eeb68fdd2c507dc6445e143`, visitors can discover mail addresses through `MEMBERS` and participant identities through OLT `WHO`, but cannot read a public profile. Resident characterization is accessible through modern application Settings, which also exposes editing and scheduling controls.

This leaves a gap in discovering familiar correspondents and conversation partners. It extends the current service subset; it is not a demonstrated regression from the Wakaba merge.

## Expected outcome

Provide a concise, read-only Japanese profile view for existing fictional residents:

- Mail: `MEMBERS` → `PROFILE recipient` → continued use of the same mailbox.
- DAISIZEN and Wakaba OLT directories: `WHO` → `PROFILE identity` → continued directory navigation.
- Inside either OLT context: `/WHO` → `/PROFILE identity` → continued quiet reading or speech in the same room.

Show only the current safe handle, existing synthetic identity token, fictional occupation and interests. Reading requires neither human registration nor model consent. Unsupported members receive an unavailable-profile response.

Command names, fields, lookup conventions, placement and presentation are category D reconstruction, not recovered 1996 host controls.

## Context

Implementation inspected read-only:

- [src/commands.ts](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/blob/b75606a0ca47d62d5eeb68fdd2c507dc6445e143/src/commands.ts): `printAddresses()` lists existing resident destinations; mailbox dispatch has no profile operation. Composer, recipient entry, registration and Settings editing already own their respective input states.
- [src/olt.ts](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/blob/b75606a0ca47d62d5eeb68fdd2c507dc6445e143/src/olt.ts): attendance displays tokens and safe names. In-room slash operations are distinguished from ordinary speech; directory input is also consumed here.
- [src/ai/personas.ts](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/blob/b75606a0ca47d62d5eeb68fdd2c507dc6445e143/src/ai/personas.ts) supplies saved/default occupations and interests. Member records supply current identity/name relationships. [src/member-presentation.ts](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/blob/b75606a0ca47d62d5eeb68fdd2c507dc6445e143/src/member-presentation.ts) supplies the established token algorithm and safe-name handling.
- Member handles in imported backups can exceed resident-editor limits. Bound profile display locally without changing stored values or existing identity algorithms.

Historical research, inspected 2026-10-24:

- [まいとーく client-author description](https://www.vector.co.jp/soft/win95/net/se024554.html) explicitly lists specified-ID handle/profile retrieval and retrieval of OLT participants' profiles. Confidence is high in these stated capabilities. Release dating and applicability throughout 1996 remain unresolved; client features do not authenticate host syntax, fields or access rules.
- [Participant archive introduction](https://toshiou1048.sakura.ne.jp/pctc_3.pdf), dated November 10, 2003 and introducing 1989–1994 records, recalls explanatory information published in a PC-VAN profile. This independently supports the profile concept with moderate historical confidence. Its damaged extraction supplies no target-year layout or command sequence.
- [LOGBOY description](https://www.vector.co.jp/soft/win31/net/se019325.html) has an indexed author description mentioning profile viewing and importing profiles from logs. Direct retrieval failed; retain as supplementary snippet-only evidence.
- [Client catalog](https://www.vector.co.jp/vpack/filearea/win95/net/comm/pcvan) exposes version 2.31 with publication label `22.10.05` in indexed results. Direct catalog and package-metadata retrieval failed. This does not date the documented capabilities to 1996.
- An apparent `PF` example occurs in an explicitly titled [novel](https://ameblo.jp/only-01/entry-12964437709.html). Exclude it from command authentication.

Reconstruction judgment: moderate confidence in adding profile discovery to the circa-1996 experience; low confidence in its exact interface. Use the existing fictional data as an explicit public projection. Occupation/interests are selected implementation fields, not authenticated historical field requirements. Anonymous access is an application reconstruction. Keep these qualifications in existing research and About/Details documentation.

[Issue #47](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/47) separates application configuration from service participation; [#52](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/52) and [#53](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/53) establish shared resident identities for mail and OLT. Profile reading should preserve those boundaries.

Live open-Issue/open-PR searches returned no items. English/Japanese profile-history searches and a profile-lookup PR search found no equivalent handoff. These searches are terminology-dependent and inventory can change.

[PR #114](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/pull/114) and `docs/validation.md` report 103 focused and 424 complete-suite checks passing with three workers, including configured type checking/build. Default/eight-worker reliability remains unresolved. These are Coordinator records assessed by this research graph; this graph ran no application checks.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Implement the three journeys above using one small shared lookup/public-projection implementation. Support current/old MAIN mail and existing SIG mail routes. Profile output preserves the selected mailbox, OLT directory/room and navigation parent.
- [ ] Accept resident destination keys shown by `MEMBERS`, existing `SYN-...` display tokens, and unique current safe handles. Define deterministic explicit-key/token precedence and reject ambiguous matches without choosing by array order. Preserve handle text and internal spaces when parsing arguments. Token lookup is presentation-only: do not change mail addressing, authentication or token generation.
- [ ] Only actual supported resident members receive occupations/interests. Use current member names and current saved resident fields; retain existing default-profile fallback where appropriate. Missing residents in restored worlds remain missing. Human members, unsupported AI members, unknown identities and external `INET#` addresses receive concise unavailable feedback without creating records or inferring biographies. Missing arguments show usage.
- [ ] Whitelist the four public fields. Do not dump the internal `profile` instruction field, routines, schedules, affinities, activity weights, preferred-board keys, private mail or other settings. Reuse identity/name helpers unchanged. Output remains bounded, literal terminal text, including markup-like custom values and unusually long imported handles; stored content remains unchanged.
- [ ] Add discoverable guidance to mail `MEMBERS` and relevant OLT help. Outside rooms use `PROFILE`; inside rooms use `/PROFILE`. Plain `PROFILE ...` remains ordinary OLT speech, and escaped `//PROFILE ...` retains existing slash-speech behavior. Lookup never sends chat or leaves/rejoins a room. Existing composer, recipient-entry, registration, confirmation and Settings-editor input ownership remains intact.
- [ ] Lookup itself performs no writes, inference, model loading, turn reservation, allowance consumption or attendance refresh. Preserve existing background OLT behavior and cancellation safeguards. A delayed lookup must not print stale data after reset/restore or a context replacement; reuse existing invalidation conventions.
- [ ] Add focused checks with existing Playwright/source-module facilities for anonymous/no-consent reading, all mail routes, both OLT contexts, directory/in-room lookup, continued navigation/speech/composition, missing/unsupported/ambiguous identities, renamed and customized residents, literal bounded output and absent restored residents. Compare protected records under controlled background timing to prove lookup has no mutation side effects; ordinary command-history bookkeeping may continue.
- [ ] Preserve existing functional, storage/backup, consent, IME, terminal rendering/logging, mail-addressing and OLT regression coverage. Suitable existing files include `tests/mail.spec.ts`, `tests/mail-presentation.spec.ts`, `tests/olt.spec.ts`, `tests/wakaba-olt.spec.ts`, `tests/composition.spec.ts` and their helpers. No new framework, schema, model or persistence subsystem is needed.
- [ ] Update relevant README/help, `docs/research/pcvan-1996-1997.md` and existing About/Details with inspected sources, access limitations, public-field selection and reconstruction confidence. Keep routine terminal output concise. Copy no archived identities, profiles or messages.
- [ ] Before merge, the Coordinator runs focused coverage and the documented complete workflow, using `npm test -- --workers=3` where the existing worker limitation applies. This configuration includes TypeScript checking and production build. Check documentation links, run `git diff --check`, review the final diff, and record actual results, failures and skipped checks without claiming default-worker reliability is resolved.

## Optional validation

Additional dated PC-VAN manuals/session evidence may refine field choices, wording or controls. Former-user feedback and native Japanese IME checks are useful but are not completion gates. No real-model execution is necessary for this deterministic feature.

## Required post-merge verification

None required. All acceptance checks are achievable before merge.

Evaluation baseline: `b75606a0ca47d62d5eeb68fdd2c507dc6445e143`.
